subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the young woman whose facial identity, long wavy dark-brown hair, and costume come from <Picture 2> — a white lace off-shoulder cropped top with a long white ribbon bow hanging down the front, a mustard-yellow and brown plaid pleated skirt with a white waistband and dark buttons, a slim silver bracelet on her right wrist, and small earrings — and whose dance performance, body movements and timing come from <Video 1>. In <Picture 2> both of her hands are raised as loose empty fists and she holds nothing; in the target video her left hand closes around the neck of <Subject 2> in place of that empty fist, while her right hand stays a free loose fist.
<Subject 2> is the whisky bottle shown in <Picture 1>, reproduced exactly as it appears there, never redesigned, restyled or re-proportioned. It is a very tall and slender clear glass bottle of 700ml capacity, its overall height about 3.1 times its widest body diameter, with straight sides that taper only very slightly toward a thick flat base, gently rounded shoulders and a short narrow neck. Its mouth is closed by a single solid natural cork stopper in pale beige-tan with fine wood grain, whose top edge is softly rounded and whose diameter is a little wider than the neck; just below the cork sits a narrow horizontal band formed by the glass bead of the mouth, reading pale silver-grey. There is no metal capsule, no foil wrap, no screw cap, no wax seal, no red band and no metallic finish anywhere on the closure. Around the shoulder a ring of faint raised glass lettering is embossed in a gentle arc, visible only as soft highlights. The glass is filled with deep amber-gold whisky right up to the shoulder, so the bottle is almost full and only the neck above the shoulder remains empty clear glass. A paper label in warm khaki-tan, a muted caramel-beige and not white, wraps the lower two thirds of the body: at the top a very large dark near-black serif wordmark sits above a fine horizontal rule, below that rule a second line in serif capitals, then a second fine rule, then two short bold serif lines, then a few lines of small print, then a tall large numeral at the lower left with tiny text beneath it, then a long horizontal rule, then a dense block of small print, and at the bottom edge the volume marking on the left and the alcohol strength on the right. On the right side of the label, occupying about one third of its height, sits a small vertically elongated oval emblem drawn in thin concentric orange-red outlines with an abstract mark inside. The label is fully wrapped and flat against the glass, with no glare masking its type. In the target video it is held upright by <Subject 1>'s left hand, which closes around the narrow neck so that four fingers wrap the right side of the neck and the thumb presses the left side.
<Subject 3> is the night-time indoor setting of <Video 1>, with a floor-to-ceiling window behind the dancer showing scattered city lights at night, a taupe curtain on the left, a row of small potted plants on the windowsill, and warm indoor lighting falling from the front.
<Video 1> is the motion reference for the target video. It supplies the dance choreography, the body and limb movement, the weight shifts and the second-by-second timing, together with its synchronized audio track.
<Audio 1> is the synchronized audio track of <Video 1> and is reused 1:1 as the complete final audio track of the target video.

summary:
[reference generation + audio reuse] The target video makes <Subject 1> re-perform, in full, the dance from <Video 1> while holding <Subject 2> in her left hand, inside <Subject 3>, in a single continuous vertical take. Because the source choreography is performed with two free hands, the routine is split: her right hand carries the complete paw-gesture sequence from <Video 1>, while her left hand holds the bottle and only echoes the vertical bounce, so the bottle stays upright, readable and inside frame throughout. The bottle is carried over from <Picture 1> unchanged, and only motion and music come from <Video 1>.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the facial identity, long wavy dark-brown hair, white lace off-shoulder cropped top with its long front ribbon bow, mustard-yellow plaid pleated skirt with white waistband, silver bracelet and small earrings from <Picture 2> are retained unchanged, while her choreography follows <Video 1>.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - every visible detail of the bottle in <Picture 1> is carried over without change: the 3.1-to-1 slender proportion, the straight sides and thick flat base, the soft shoulders and short narrow neck, the solid pale beige-tan natural cork stopper with its rounded top and its slightly wider diameter than the neck, the narrow pale silver-grey glass bead band beneath the cork, the faint ring of raised embossed lettering across the shoulder, the deep amber-gold whisky filled right up to the shoulder, the warm khaki-tan label covering the lower two thirds with its large dark serif wordmark, its two fine rules, its two bold serif lines, its small numeral block and its long rule, the small vertically elongated orange-red concentric oval emblem on the right, and the volume and strength markings at the bottom edge. The closure never becomes metal, foil, screw-cap, wax or red, the fill level never rises or falls, the label never turns white and never changes its type or layout, and the bottle is never released, opened, poured or drunk from.
<Subject 3> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the night window with city lights, the taupe curtain, the potted plants on the windowsill and the warm frontal indoor lighting are retained.
<Video 1> (dance motion and timing): attribute_transfer - the full-body dance choreography, the arm and hand gesture sequence, the hip sways, head tilts, weight shifts and the second-by-second timing are transferred onto <Subject 1>, while the original performer's identity, costume, environment and audio are not carried over.
<Audio 1>: fully_copy - <Audio 1> is reused 1:1 as the target video's complete final audio track.

detailed_description:
The target video is a realistic vertical smartphone home-dance clip in a casual, un-staged style, lit warmly from the front, framed as one continuous shot with no cuts. <Audio 1> plays from the first frame at an unchanged tempo and every bounce lands on its beat.
[Shot 1] The frame opens with <Subject 1> seen from behind at the centre of <Subject 3>, her long wavy dark-brown hair falling down her back, her right arm bent with a loose fist lifted near shoulder level, and <Subject 2> held low at her left side. Within the first half-second she pivots on the spot to face the camera, her hair and the long white ribbon sweeping outward with the turn and motion blur trailing across the rotation. She settles into a frontal medium shot framed from head to mid-thigh, the night window and its scattered city lights behind her, the taupe curtain at the left edge, the potted plants at the lower right.
From about 00:01.000 she runs the source choreography on the beat of <Audio 1>. Her right hand carries the full gesture: the elbow bends and the loose fist rises to beside her right cheek, opening and closing four times in time with the beat while her shoulder bounces. Her left hand keeps <Subject 2> gripped by its neck — four fingers around the right side of the narrow neck, the thumb pressing the left side — and drives it through the same small vertical bounce as the original fist, so the bottle stays upright beside her left shoulder at a constant height, never dipping toward the bottom of frame and never crossing in front of her face, with the khaki-tan label fully uncovered and turned toward the camera. The bottle looks exactly as it does in <Picture 1> and never changes: the closure stays a bare pale beige-tan cork with its narrow silver-grey glass bead beneath, the shoulder keeps its faint ring of raised embossed lettering, the whisky stays filled right up to the shoulder, the label keeps its warm khaki-tan tone and its dark serif wordmark, and the small orange-red concentric oval emblem stays small and sharp on the right of the label. There is only ever one bottle in the frame, still in her hand, never duplicated and never floating.
Through the middle of the take she adds the source video's hip sways and head tilts: her head tips to one side and swings back, her right fist drops to brush her chin and cheek in a small beckoning gesture and returns to its raised position three times, the pleats of her plaid skirt flare and close with each sway, and the white ribbon swings across her midriff. Her left arm stays quiet, letting the bottle travel only a few centimetres with the body, and the gripped neck remains the fixed point that keeps it vertical.
Later the sways widen: her torso leans left and recovers, then leans right and recovers, her hair lifts off her shoulders and swings across her back, and the white ribbon sweeps almost horizontally to the side before falling back. Her right fist pumps upward twice, and her left arm lifts the bottle slightly and settles it back to the same height. She keeps her eyes on the lens throughout, alternating a closed-lip smile with an open-mouthed grin as if mouthing along to the music, with no intelligible words. The clip ends with her facing the camera, right fist still raised and <Subject 2> upright beside her left shoulder with the label still uncovered and readable, and neither her costume, her hair nor any part of the bottle has changed since the first frame.

overall_soundscape:
The ambience layer copied from <Audio 1> runs through the whole video, carrying the original take's room tone and light fabric rustle, with no dialogue and no narration.

non_diegetic_music:
<Audio 1> is directly reused as the complete audience-only score, with nothing added, removed, re-timed or replaced.
